lesson_scope: Equilibrium of smooth rings and beads threaded on horizontal, vertical, and circular wires; uniform tension in light continuous strings passing around smooth pulleys and through smooth rings; normal reaction perpendicular to guides and wire surfaces; resultant forces on pulley brackets and pins; movable pulley mechanical advantage; and asymmetrical deflection and relaxation geometry.

Determine the support needed from the wire:
- Because the pull only provides $5\text{ N}$ of lift, the wire must supply the remaining $1\text{ N}$ of upward support:
$$R_N = 6 - 5 = 1\text{ N}$$

$$\text{Tension is constant along the string}$$

Balance the hanging mass:
- The vertical segment holds a $3\text{ kg}$ mass, giving tension $30\text{ N}$:
$$P = T = 3 \times 10 = 30\text{ N}$$

- This corresponds to a $5-12-13$ right-angled triangle, so $\cos\alpha = \frac{12}{13}$.

$$R_N = 13\cos\alpha = 13 \times \frac{12}{13} = 12\text{ N}$$

- Equal base angles:
$$\angle CAB = \angle CBA = \frac{60^\circ}{2} = 30^\circ$$
The string forms a $30^\circ$ angle with the vertical and with radius $CB$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 5: Smooth bead on fixed vertical circular wire

hints: Resolving along the tangent to the circle is ideal because the normal reaction $R_N$ acts along the radius and has zero tangential component.

The tangent is perpendicular to radius $CB$. Because radius $CB$ is at $60^\circ$ to the downward vertical, the tangent is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the vertical, so the tangential component of weight is $4\sin 60^\circ = 2\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.

String $AB$ makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with radius $CB$, so it makes $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$ with the tangent. Balance tangentially: $T\cos 60^\circ = 4\sin 60^\circ \implies 0.5 T = 2\sqrt{3} \implies T = 4\sqrt{3} \approx 6.93\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify components along the tangent to the circle at point $B$:
- The normal reaction $R_N$ acts along the radius, so its component along the tangent is zero.
- Downward weight $W = 4\text{ N}$ acts at angle $60^\circ$ to the normal, so its tangential component is $4\sin 60^\circ = 2\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.
- String $AB$ makes angle $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$ with the tangent:
$$T\cos 60^\circ = 4\sin 60^\circ$$

Solve for the string tension $T$:
$$T(0.5) = 4\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 2\sqrt{3} \implies T = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 4(1.73205) = 6.9282 \approx 6.93\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Eliminate the unknown reaction by resolving tangentially:
- The wire pushes purely along the radius, so $R_N$ disappears from the tangential balance.
- Tangential pull of gravity:
$$W_\text{tangent} = 4\sin 60^\circ = 2\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Balance with the string tension:
- The string pulls at $60^\circ$ to the tangent:
$$T\cos 60^\circ = 2\sqrt{3} \implies 0.5 T = 2\sqrt{3} \implies T = 4\sqrt{3} \approx 6.93\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves tangentially (eliminating normal reaction $R_N$): $T\cos 60^\circ = 4\sin 60^\circ$.
Solves $T(0.5) = 4\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ to obtain $T = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 6.93\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 5: Smooth bead on fixed vertical circular wire

hints: Resolve forces along the radius $CB$.
The inward radial component of tension is $T\cos 30^\circ = 4\sqrt{3}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 6\text{ N}$.
The inward radial component of weight is $4\cos 60^\circ = 4(0.5) = 2\text{ N}$.
Since the string pulls inwards with $6\text{ N}$ while weight only provides $2\text{ N}$ outwards along $CB$, the wire must push radially outwards with $6 - 2 = 4\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify forces acting along the radius $CB$:
- String tension pulls inwards towards $A$ at angle $30^\circ$ to the radius:
$$T_\text{radial} = T\cos 30^\circ = (4\sqrt{3})\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 6\text{ N}$$
- Weight has component along $CB$:
$$W_\text{radial} = 4\cos 60^\circ = 2\text{ N}$$

Set up radial equilibrium for the normal reaction $R_N$ (assumed inwards towards $C$):
$$\Sigma F_\text{radial} = R_N + T\cos 30^\circ - 4\cos 60^\circ = 0$$
$$R_N + 6 - 2 = 0 \implies R_N = -4\text{ N}$$

Conclude the magnitude and physical direction:
The negative sign indicates that the normal reaction acts in the opposite direction, namely radially outwards from centre $C$, with magnitude $4\text{ N}$:
$$R_N = 4\text{ N} \quad (\text{radially outwards})$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Sum the forces directed along the radius $CB$:
- String pulls strongly inwards towards $C$:
$$T_\text{radial} = 4\sqrt{3}\cos 30^\circ = 6\text{ N}$$
- Gravity pulls partially outwards away from $C$:
$$W_\text{radial} = 4\cos 60^\circ = 2\text{ N}$$

Determine the wire's resistance:
- Inward pull ($6\text{ N}$) exceeds outward gravity component ($2\text{ N}$).
- The wire must push outwards to prevent the bead from cutting into the circle:
$$R_N = 6 - 2 = 4\text{ N} \quad (\text{radially outwards})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up radial equilibrium along $CB$: $R_N + T\cos 30^\circ = 4\cos 60^\circ$ or equivalent radial balance.
Substitutes $T = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ to evaluate $R_N = 2 - 6 = -4\text{ N}$, giving magnitude $4\text{ N}$.
States clearly that the normal reaction acts radially outwards from centre $C$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 1: Movable pulley system with variable support angles

hints: The string is continuous and passes around smooth pulleys, so the tension $T$ is identical everywhere along the string.
The movable pulley is supported by two vertical segments of the same string, each pulling upwards with tension $T$.
Balance the movable pulley vertically: $2 T = W = 24\text{ N} \implies T = 12\text{ N}$.
The counterweight hangs in vertical equilibrium from the other end of the string, so $mg = T = 12\text{ N} \implies m = 1.2\text{ kg}$.

walkthrough.text:
Explain why tension is uniform:
Because the string is light and inextensible, and both pulleys $P$ and $B$ are frictionless and smooth, there are no tangential frictional forces to alter the tension along the string:
$$\text{Tension } T \text{ is uniform everywhere}$$

Resolve forces vertically on the movable pulley:
Both parallel segments pull upwards:
$$\Sigma F_y = 2 T - Mg = 0$$
$$2 T = 2.4(10) = 24 \implies T = 12\text{ N}$$

Find the counterweight mass $m$:
$$\Sigma F_y = mg - T = 0 \implies 10 m = 12 \implies m = 1.2\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Understand the mechanical advantage of a movable pulley:
- Two upward vertical strands share the $24\text{ N}$ load:
$$2 T = 24\text{ N} \implies T = 12\text{ N}$$

Determine the counterweight mass:
- The tension required at the free end is cut in half:
$$m = \frac{12}{10} = 1.2\text{ kg}$$
A $1.2\text{ kg}$ counterweight balances a $2.4\text{ kg}$ load.

ai_rubric.observable: States that because the string is light and both pulleys are smooth and frictionless, the tension $T$ is uniform throughout.
Resolves vertically on the movable pulley: $2 T = 24 \implies T = 12\text{ N}$.
Equates counterweight to tension: $mg = 12 \implies m = 1.2\text{ kg}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 1: Movable pulley system with variable support angles

hints: Resolve vertically on the movable pulley with the segments at $45^\circ$ to the vertical: $2 T'\cos 45^\circ = 24 \implies T'\sqrt{2} = 24 \implies T' = 12\sqrt{2} \approx 17.0\text{ N}$.
The counterweight hangs vertically from the string, so $m' = \frac{T'}{g} = \frac{12\sqrt{2}}{10} = 1.2\sqrt{2} \approx 1.70\text{ kg}$.
At the fixed pulley $B$, one string segment pulls towards the movable pulley (down and left at $45^\circ$ to the vertical) and the other pulls straight down.

Find the horizontal and vertical components on pulley $B$: $F_x = T'\sin 45^\circ = 12\text{ N}$ and $F_y = T'\cos 45^\circ + T' = 12 + 12\sqrt{2} \approx 28.97\text{ N}$. Then compute $R_B = \sqrt{12^2 + 28.97^2} \approx 31.4\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces vertically on the movable pulley with angled segments:
$$\Sigma F_y = 2 T'\cos 45^\circ - 24 = 0$$
$$2 T'\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 24 \implies T'\sqrt{2} = 24$$
$$T' = \frac{24}{\sqrt{2}} = 12\sqrt{2}\text{ N} \approx 12(1.41421) = 16.9706 \approx 17.0\text{ N}$$

Find the new counterweight mass $m'$:
$$m' = \frac{T'}{g} = \frac{12\sqrt{2}}{10} = 1.2\sqrt{2}\text{ kg} \approx 1.697 \approx 1.70\text{ kg}$$

Determine the orthogonal components of the resultant force on fixed pulley $B$:
- Horizontal component:
$$F_x = T'\sin 45^\circ = (12\sqrt{2})\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 12\text{ N}$$
- Vertical component (both pulling downwards):
$$F_y = T'\cos 45^\circ + T' = 12 + 12\sqrt{2} \approx 12 + 16.9706 = 28.9706\text{ N}$$

Calculate the resultant force magnitude $R_B$:
$$R_B = \sqrt{F_x^2 + F_y^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + 28.9706^2} = \sqrt{144 + 839.293} = \sqrt{983.293} \approx 31.357 \approx 31.4\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Analyze the effect of spreading the ropes:
- The angled strands lose vertical efficiency:
$$2 T'\cos 45^\circ = 24\text{ N} \implies T' = 12\sqrt{2} \approx 17.0\text{ N}$$
- The tension increases from $12\text{ N}$ to $17.0\text{ N}$.

Adjust the counterweight:
- A heavier counterweight is needed to hold the steeper tension:
$$m' = 1.2\sqrt{2} \approx 1.70\text{ kg}$$

Calculate the force on fixed pulley $B$:
- Sideways pull to the left: $12\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ = 12\text{ N}$.
- Downward pull: $12\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ + 12\sqrt{2} = 12 + 16.97 = 28.97\text{ N}$:
$$F_x = 12\text{ N}, \quad F_y = 28.97\text{ N}$$

Combine components into total bracket load:
$$R_B = \sqrt{12^2 + 28.97^2} \approx 31.4\text{ N}$$
The fixed pulley axle supports a resultant force of $31.4\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertically on the movable pulley: $2 T'\cos 45^\circ = 24$.
Obtains $T' = 12\sqrt{2}\text{ N} \approx 17.0\text{ N}$ and $m' = 1.2\sqrt{2}\text{ kg} \approx 1.70\text{ kg}$.
Resolves string forces on fixed pulley $B$: $F_x = T'\sin 45^\circ = 12\text{ N}$ and $F_y = T'\cos 45^\circ + T' = 12 + 12\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$.
Calculates resultant magnitude $R_B = \sqrt{12^2 + (12 + 12\sqrt{2})^2} \approx 31.4\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Capstone Practice 2: Smooth ring on string with applied horizontal load and relaxation geometry

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Smooth ring on string with applied horizontal load and relaxation geometry

hints: A smooth ring slides freely along the string without friction, ensuring that the tension $T$ is identical in both segments $AR$ and $BR$.
Resolve forces vertically: both string segments pull upwards to support the $12\text{ N}$ weight: $T\cos 60^\circ + T\cos 30^\circ = 12$.
Factor out $T$: $T\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 12 \implies T\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{2}\right) = 12$.
Rationalize the denominator: $T = \frac{24}{\sqrt{3} + 1} = \frac{24(\sqrt{3} - 1)}{2} = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1) \approx 8.78\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Explain uniform tension:
Because the ring is smooth, there are no frictional forces tangential to the string, so the tension $T$ is uniform throughout both segments $AR$ and $BR$:
$$T_{AR} = T_{BR} = T$$

Form the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$\Sigma F_y = T\cos 60^\circ + T\cos 30^\circ - 12 = 0$$
$$T\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 12 \implies T\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{2}\right) = 12$$

Solve for the exact tension $T$:
$$T = \frac{24}{\sqrt{3} + 1} = \frac{24(\sqrt{3} - 1)}{(\sqrt{3} + 1)(\sqrt{3} - 1)} = \frac{24(\sqrt{3} - 1)}{2} = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1)\text{ N}$$
$$T \approx 12(0.73205) = 8.7846 \approx 8.78\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Establish the single tension property:
- The smooth ring equalizes tension across both segments:
$$T_{AR} = T_{BR} = T$$

Sum the upward vertical pulls:
- Segment $AR$ provides $T\cos 60^\circ = 0.5 T$.
- Segment $BR$ provides $T\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} T$:
$$T\left(\frac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 12\text{ N}$$

Rationalize the exact result:
$$T = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1) \approx 8.78\text{ N}$$
The string tension is $8.78\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: States that because the ring is smooth and frictionless, the tension $T$ is uniform across both segments of the string.
Resolves vertically in equilibrium: $T\cos 60^\circ + T\cos 30^\circ = 12$.
Solves $T\left(\frac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 12$ to obtain $T = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1)\text{ N} \approx 8.78\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Smooth ring on string with applied horizontal load and relaxation geometry

hints: Examine horizontal forces at ring $R$: pulling force $P$ acts to the right, segment $BR$ pulls to the right with $T\sin 30^\circ$, and segment $AR$ pulls to the left with $T\sin 60^\circ$.
Set up horizontal balance: $P + T\sin 30^\circ = T\sin 60^\circ \implies P = T(\sin 60^\circ - \sin 30^\circ) = T\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2}\right)$.
Substitute the exact value $T = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1)$ into the formula for $P$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up horizontal force equilibrium at ring $R$:
Segment $AR$ pulls leftwards with $T\sin 60^\circ$, while segment $BR$ pulls rightwards with $T\sin 30^\circ$ and force $P$ pulls rightwards:
$$\Sigma F_x = P + T\sin 30^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ = 0$$
$$P = T(\sin 60^\circ - \sin 30^\circ) = T\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2}\right)$$

Substitute the exact expression for $T = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1)$:
$$P = [12(\sqrt{3} - 1)]\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2}\right) = 6(\sqrt{3} - 1)^2$$
$$P = 6(3 - 2\sqrt{3} + 1) = 6(4 - 2\sqrt{3}) = 24 - 12\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Evaluate the numerical value of $P$:
$$P \approx 24 - 12(1.73205) = 24 - 20.7846 = 3.2154 \approx 3.22\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Balance the horizontal pulls:
- Leftward pull from $AR$: $T\sin 60^\circ$.
- Rightward pull from $BR$: $T\sin 30^\circ$.
- Applied pull $P$ assists to the right:
$$P = T(\sin 60^\circ - \sin 30^\circ) = T\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2}\right)$$

Substitute the tension expression:
- Notice the beautiful squaring of $(\sqrt{3} - 1)$:
$$P = 6(\sqrt{3} - 1)^2 = 6(4 - 2\sqrt{3}) = 24 - 12\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Evaluate the pulling force:
$$P \approx 3.22\text{ N}$$
A modest horizontal pull of $3.22\text{ N}$ creates the asymmetric deflection.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves horizontally in equilibrium: $P + T\sin 30^\circ = T\sin 60^\circ$.
Expresses $P = T(\sin 60^\circ - \sin 30^\circ) = T\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2}\right)$.
Evaluates $P = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2}\right) = 6(\sqrt{3} - 1)^2 = 24 - 12\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 3.22\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Smooth ring on string with applied horizontal load and relaxation geometry

hints: Without any horizontal force, the smooth ring slides to the center, creating two equal string segments of length $\frac{2.0}{2} = 1.0\text{ m}$.
The ceiling span is $1.2\text{ m}$, so the horizontal half-span is $\frac{1.2}{2} = 0.6\text{ m}$.
Use Pythagoras theorem to find the vertical sag depth: $h = \sqrt{1.0^2 - 0.6^2} = \sqrt{1.00 - 0.36} = \sqrt{0.64} = 0.8\text{ m}$.
Resolve vertically in symmetrical equilibrium: $2 T_0\sin\alpha = 12$, where $\sin\alpha = \frac{h}{1.0} = 0.8$, giving $1.6 T_0 = 12 \implies T_0 = 7.5\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the symmetrical geometry when $P = 0$:
By symmetry, the ring hangs directly below the midpoint of $AB$:
$$\text{Segment length } L_s = \frac{2.0}{2} = 1.0\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Half-span } d = \frac{1.2}{2} = 0.6\text{ m}$$

Calculate the vertical sag depth $h$ using Pythagoras theorem:
$$h = \sqrt{L_s^2 - d^2} = \sqrt{1.0^2 - 0.6^2} = \sqrt{1.00 - 0.36} = \sqrt{0.64} = 0.8\text{ m}$$

Resolve vertically in symmetrical equilibrium to find the new tension $T_0$:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{h}{L_s} = \frac{0.8}{1.0} = 0.8$$
$$\Sigma F_y = 2 T_0\sin\alpha - 12 = 0$$
$$2 T_0(0.8) = 12 \implies 1.6 T_0 = 12 \implies T_0 = \frac{12}{1.6} = 7.5\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the natural resting geometry:
- Without the sideways pull, the ring centers itself.
- Hypotenuse is $1.0\text{ m}$, horizontal half-base is $0.6\text{ m}$:
$$h = \sqrt{1.0^2 - 0.6^2} = 0.8\text{ m}$$

Evaluate the vertical inclination ratio:
- Each segment rises with ratio:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{0.8}{1.0} = 0.8$$

Calculate the relaxed tension:
- Both strands lift together to support the $12\text{ N}$ weight:
$$2 T_0(0.8) = 12 \implies 1.6 T_0 = 12 \implies T_0 = 7.5\text{ N}$$
The tension drops from $8.78\text{ N}$ to $7.5\text{ N}$ as the system relaxes to symmetry.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies symmetrical lengths: each segment has length $1.0\text{ m}$ and half-span $0.6\text{ m}$, calculating depth $h = \sqrt{1.0^2 - 0.6^2} = 0.8\text{ m}$.
Obtains $h = 0.8\text{ m}$.
Resolves vertically: $2 T_0\left(\frac{0.8}{1.0}\right) = 12 \implies 1.6 T_0 = 12 \implies T_0 = 7.5\text{ N}$.
